original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: Whether every weight-1 no-edge pool of pattern dimension 4 and joint-image dimension 4 is reducible.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a larger or nonabelian register alphabet. This package instead answers open question 2 of #7138: the weight-1 no-edge pools of pattern dimension 4 whose joint image has dimension 4, which the kernel test does not reach. No new alphabet, word, or kappa is claimed. The same card was already moved to scalar pattern-pool questions by #5921, #6838, #6921, #6962, and #7138.
bottleneck_link: Side result. The weight-1 image bound does not decide reducibility when the joint image has dimension equal to the pattern dimension. This package does not open a new register-alphabet construction round, and the family expansion gate is not used. The original native acceptance gate remains unmet, and the selected frontier is unchanged.
stop_rule: Stop once one explicit weight-1 no-edge pool of pattern dimension 4 and joint-image dimension 4 is proved irreducible at every width at least 4, and the four disjoint weight-1 lines are rechecked as reducible. Do not classify all such pools, redo the image-at-most-6 theorem, or change kappa.
evidence: PROOF.md exhibits the transpose of the #6962 four-cycle and proves that it is a complete weight-1 no-edge pool of pattern dimension 4 acting irreducibly on a four-dimensional joint image at every width at least 4. verify.py repeats the finite tables, the width-4 through width-8 pool scan, the 67-subspace lattice, and the reducible four-line and deleted-projector controls.

open_questions.question: Which weight-1 no-edge pools of pattern dimension 4 and joint-image dimension 4 are irreducible, up to coordinate permutation?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The transpose four-cycle is irreducible, while the four disjoint weight-1 lines are reducible. Both have pattern dimension 4, image dimension 4, and trivial common kernel, so neither a single witness nor the kernel test classifies the boundary.
open_questions.first_step: Use the four-column lemma in PROOF.md: any irreducible example has exactly four columns of dimension 1. Enumerate the 4096 matrices over F2 with ones on the diagonal, keep the invertible strongly connected ones, and decide which admit extra coordinates that preserve weight-1 covectors and exclude matrix units. Write the completeness argument before calling the list a census.
open_questions.blocked_by: This package does not enumerate those matrices. Extra coordinates are not bounded here, so the 4096 matrices are not yet an exhaustive domain. A partial list would not be a classification.
